speaker: interviewer
text: Hey Liam, thanks for hopping on. How's it going?

speaker: interviewee
text: Good, good. Just got back from a run, so if I'm out of breath, that's why.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, no problem. So, no wrong answers, just about your grocery orders.

speaker: interviewee
text: Cool.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: It's me and my girlfriend Noor, in a flat near the park. I'm a PE teacher, she's a nurse, so our hours are kind of opposite. Whoever's free does the shop. Usually it's me, on the bike, to the supermarket on the high street.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: Noor's sister uses it, I think. Or she'd heard of it. Something like that.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: Opened it, typed stuff in. Pasta, oats, bananas, eggs, a big bag of rice, tins, hot chocolate. Paid. Then just waited around, watched the little car on the map.

speaker: interviewer
text: And was anything confusing?

speaker: interviewee
text: Not really. Took me a minute to find the eggs, they were under dairy, which, okay.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Once? Twice maybe. Not a lot.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: The oats, I think. I got a different brand, like the jumbo ones. Didn't matter, oats are oats.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did they let you know before it arrived?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, there was a message saying they'd replaced something. I saw it, I just didn't care.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I took whatever was there. I think they only had one slot that day, the evening one.

speaker: interviewer
text: And on a normal week, would you be home for a two-hour slot?

speaker: interviewee
text: On a school day, no way. I'm at work till five and then I've got the after-school club.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Nah. I don't use it enough. If it was like two a month, I might forget about it and keep it.

speaker: interviewer
text: What if it was 9.99 a month for free delivery?

speaker: interviewee
text: Ten a month? No, I'd cancel it straight away.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Okay. What did you like most about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Honestly, that it turned up at all. That was the two days the whole street was snowed in, the buses stopped, I wasn't getting the bike out in that, so it was the app or eating tins. Once the roads were clear I was back on the bike to the high street.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, I guess. It worked fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The app asks for a lot of permissions. Location, notifications, contacts. Why contacts?

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was it overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Seven, eight. Solid.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Did Noor use it as well?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, she just ate the hot chocolate.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Have you seen the recipes section?

speaker: interviewee
text: No. I just make pasta.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: Nope, I think that's it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Thanks so much Liam, this was really helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: No worries, see you.
